newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest hogs seen steady-$0.50 lower - dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest hogs seen steady-$0.50 lower - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Thursday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by outlooks for more than adequate hog marketings, livestock dealers said.
Higher prices on Wednesday and rain in Iowa reportedly brought in more than enough hogs to fill the reduced needs of packers who continue to cut back slaughter, they said.
Unprofitable operating margins have resulted in slaughter reductions for the third consecutive week.
Hog kill Wednesday was estimated at 314,000 head, down from 333,000 last week and 332,000 last year, USDA reported.
Week to date slaughter was estimated at 909,000 head, down 4.8 percent from the same period a week ago and down 9.3 percent from a year ago, USDA statistics showed.
Smaller pork production was lending support to pork prices, but packer margins were not improved because hog prices were higher on Wednesday, sources noted.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota top prices for hogs at the plant could range $57.50 to $58.00 and Illinois top prices at plant were seen ranging from $57.50 to $58.00.
Indiana/Ohio top prices at plants could span $57.00 to $57.50, dealers and packer buyers there said.
